            Apps for people outside the console, and the Builder opens what SATOM has. A Plugin Studio app can carry its own sign-in (local accounts, LDAP or FortiAuthenticator groups, two-factor) and an Apps only profile whose whole menu is its apps; apps can be filed under menu groups that become Plugins submenus; SATOM Builder lists and opens this server's plugins and apps. Scout becomes the operations assistant: it correlates logs (with optional Splunk and Elasticsearch / OpenSearch sources), Sentinel incidents, jobs and the audit log, proposes Path Diagnostics walks, and every walk is saved as a report with the metrics around it. Knowledge packs are now kbpacks, and Software Update takes the update, the API pack and the kbpack in one Upload.

            Added

            • SATOM Builder opens what this server already has (request: "I still don't see SATOM's plugins in the Builder; they should all be there"). Two read-only API routes for the Builder (contract §21): GET /api/v1/builder/plugins lists every Plugin Studio app and the Report Studio plugins of the call's ADOM, each with whether the Builder can open it and, when not, why (a script app, a code plugin, a Report Studio plugin when the token's owner is not a super-admin); GET /api/v1/builder/plugins/<kind>/<slug>/package sends one of them as the console's unsigned export (connections without secrets). The token's owner must be a Plugin Studio author. The Builder's Open from SATOM page uses them.
            • Plugin Studio apps can be filed under a menu group (request: "let plugins belong to groups, so the menu shows the groups as submenus and Studio can filter by them"). A flow app's Settings tab has a Menu group field, and every app, flow or script, has Set menu group in its row menu of Plugin Studio › Apps. Both suggest the groups that already exist; a name that differs only in case is filed under the existing group, and an empty field takes the app out. In the sidebar each group is a collapsible submenu of Plugins, open only when you are on one of its apps; apps without a group stay plain entries below the groups. Plugin Studio › Apps has a Menu group column and filter (every group, one group, no group), next to the search box. An app package carries the group (app.group, optional); an import applies it only when it creates the app, and an app that already exists keeps the group this server gave it (as with its ADOMs). Audit Log: studio.app.group; the group is also recorded in studio.app.settings. A menu group is not a user group: who may use an app is still set under Who may use it. Schema: studio_apps.menu_group (migration appgroup01).
            • Scout proposes a Path Diagnostics walk; the operator runs it (request: "do everything and leave nothing pending" — the next stage was a walk Scout asks for and the operator confirms). A new proposal kind, path_walk: Open Path Diagnostics opens the form filled in (appliance, object, Host, window) in a new tab with a note that nothing runs until Walk is pressed. The walk goes through the same route, permission and ADOM scoping as a hand-typed one; when it is saved it closes the proposal (path_report:<id>, Audit Log advisor.proposal_apply), the report links back to the conversation, and the chat shows the report to read. A proposal id edited in the URL attaches nothing (other device, other user's conversation, already applied, not a walk).
            • Settings → AI → Scout: tool rounds per question (1–12, default 6, was a fixed 4 — a full investigation needs six). When the rounds are spent Scout gets one more round without tools to answer from what it has and name the checks it could not make.
            • Log sources: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch / Wazuh indexer (_search, index pattern, API key or Basic auth, configurable time field). Scout's text is a phrase value inside a JSON query — never query_string syntax; a timed-out answer or failed shards is an error, not a quieter result. Unverified against a live cluster (the lab's only OpenSearch, the Wazuh indexer, is on a powered-off host) and labelled so.
            • Path Diagnostics: report retention (Settings → Path Diagnostics → Saved reports; default 0 = keep every report). Pruning runs when a walk is saved, never on the read-only standby.
            • Interface packets, errors and discards. The REST interface collector now also stores packets (satom_iface_{rx,tx}_packets_total; FortiWeb 8.0.6 rows carry rx/tx packet counts, read on {device}). Those rows have no error or drop field, so the SNMP collector reads IF-MIB ifIn/OutErrors, ifIn/OutDiscards and the 64-bit unicast packet counters (satom_snmp_if_*_total, skipped when the agent does not serve them — unverified on a live Fortinet SNMP agent). The Path Diagnostics metrics panel shows packets/s, errors and discards per interface and flags any error or discard in the window.
            • An app's sign-in lives in Plugin Studio and travels in its package (request: "I don't see it -- this configuration should be inside Plugin Studio so it can be added, otherwise it is harder for the user, and this part must also be registered in the Builder"). Plugin Studio → Apps → app gets a Sign-in tab (rules, Apps only profile, approval, the people who signed in, Revoke), and a script app the same tab in its script editor; Plugin Studio gets a Sign-in directories pane with the directory connections (add, edit, test). Both are the Access pages drawn in Plugin Studio: same routes, same user management permission -- an author without it sees the tab read only. app.json carries "signin" (contract section 20): connections by id and kind, the profile by name, never a server, an account, a secret or the on/off; the import brings it switched off, leaves out (with a warning and a to-do) a rule whose connection this server lacks or has with another kind, and keeps the rules an app already has. New package rules app.signin, app.signin_off, app.signin_connection; the Builder's target lists the directory connections (id and kind only) and the Apps only profiles, and the author guide describes the sign-in.
            • Scout correlates logs, incidents, jobs and the audit log (request: "do the next stage, and add an extra source where it checks logs, a Splunk or similar, as optional — for products such as Cisco we will not have the logs in the FortiAnalyzer"). New read-only tools: search_logs (the logs of ONE window from every source side by side — Sentinel events, the syslog receiver, the FortiAnalyzer behind the appliance, external SIEMs — each with a status: ok, no_match, error, not_configured, disabled or forbidden; with report_id it takes a Path Diagnostics walk's appliance and window), list_incidents / incident (Sentinel), recent_jobs / job_detail (every REST call and SSH command a job made), audit_events and recent_alerts (the operator's own bell). Each applies the gate of the page that shows the same data, as the operator. source: "all" searches every log source, a job status of failed finds the jobs that failed, and an unknown source or status is an error naming the valid values; incidents follow the Sentinel console's rule (matched by device name, incidents without a device included).
            • Settings → AI → Log sources (optional): Splunk. An administrator can point Scout at a SIEM, read only — for the non-Fortinet hops of a path. The token is stored encrypted and never shown; TLS is verified against the trust store unless switched off per source; Scout's text only ever becomes one quoted search term, so it cannot append a command; save, delete and Test leave Audit Log rows without the token. The Splunk connector is unverified against a live Splunk and says so.
            • DNS & LB Lookup as Plugin Studio apps (request: "I want the whole DNS & LB Lookup section to be an app in Plugin Studio — the page stays, and keep Copy, editing a record from its row and the decommission confirmation"). Three plugins, delivered like every other one (request: "this is a plugin, it should be handled like everything else, under the Plugins section"): signed packages of the internal plugin generator, 1.0.0 on the staging hub /downloads/plugins/, imported in Plugin Studio › Apps › Import app package and published under Operations › Plugins — DNS Records (dns-records: list, then Edit / Delete on each record, create, update, delete), Decommission a service (dns-decommission: the plan, a tick box per warning, the policy name typed back, apply) and DNS & LB Lookup (dns-lb-lookup: DNS answers per resolver, LB matches from the device cache, Quick LB, Not found; Copy DNS / Copy LB; Records, Open policy and Decommission on each row). Import dns-lb-lookup last: its DNS Records action opens dns-records, and an import that names an app the server does not have is refused with that app's name. They are not Examples templates (they can be deleted like any app). The page under Fleet › DNS Lookup is unchanged.
            • Six SATOM steps behind them, adapters over the modules the page uses: DNS: look names up, LB: match names to the fleet, DNS records: list, DNS records: create, change or delete, Decommission: plan and Decommission: apply the plan. Each asks the user who runs the app for the page route's permission (network.view, user_manage, config_write) and runs in the run's ADOM as that user, so an app never widens access or sees another ADOM's fleet; a run with no person (a schedule, an event) is refused.
            • Plugin Studio: Copy to the clipboard action (text, tab-separated table or JSON) and Open another app's form here (the form opens over the run page, filled in, and the run is followed in the same window).
            • Plugin Studio: row buttons on an Output table (Row buttons (JSON)): an app opened filled in with the row's values, or a SATOM page; when per button; no button for an app the person may not use; only SATOM paths.
            • Plugin Studio: Output "plan" view (a decommission plan: delete / unbind / keep per stage, warnings and blockers).

            • Plugin Studio: Ask a person — Must be acknowledged / Blocks the Yes answer / Type to confirm. One tick box per warning; Yes is refused on the server until every one is ticked, while a blocker stands, and until the confirmation text (the decommission app: the policy name) is typed. The answer is saved as {{ last_answer }}.

            • Apps for people outside the console, with their own sign-in (request: "I want apps that are only for a group of people, with the same login but only to this app and nothing else; and they could authenticate differently from SATOM's login — the AD query or the FortiAuthenticator group can be different, even other servers").

            • Profiles › Type: Apps only — no permission, no console: the account lands on My apps (/a/), opens only the apps given to it, and every console page and the API v1 answer not found / owner_forbidden. Deny by default: a route added later stays closed to these accounts until it is allowed on purpose (a test walks the whole URL map).
            • Access › Directory connections — any number of AD, LDAP and RADIUS/FortiAuthenticator servers, each with its own address, bind account and write-only secret, independent of Settings › Authentication.

            • Access › App sign-in — per app: its own sign-in page (/a/<app>/login, in the app's colours) with ordered rules — AD/LDAP group DNs (AD nested) and an optional LDAP filter, RADIUS Fortinet-Group-Name groups, or local accounts — each optionally requiring a SATOM authenticator code (enrolled at the first sign-in). Accounts are user@<connection>, pinned to that connection and never accepted by the console sign-in; a sign-in proves its own app only, and an administrator can revoke it at once.

            • Path Diagnostics saves every walk. Each walk is stored as a report (Saved as report #N under the verdict), listed under Latest saved reports and on /scout/reports, reopened as drawn or as JSON (/scout/reports/<id>.json), and visible exactly when its appliance is. The scout.walk audit row names the report and the job that carried the walk's device calls. New table path_diag_reports (migration pdiag01).

            • Metrics around the walk. Under the ladder, a panel reads the metrics store for the walk's own window against the seven days before it: appliance CPU, memory, sessions and new connections; the object's status, throughput, sessions, transactions and client/server/application response times; interface rates; each collector's status. Readings 2× off their 7-day average are flagged. It never changes the verdict; a failed collector or a silent store is METRICS ERROR, an appliance with no scrape target not collected. An interface that lacks a reading (no SNMP counters, no packet counters on a FortiADC) shows an empty cell instead of failing the page.
            • Scout is the operations assistant. Its prompt now puts finding and resolving faults first (newest Path Diagnostics report → metrics → device health → recent changes; evidence kept apart from inference; missing data said in words), and three read-only tools feed it: list_path_reports, path_report and metrics_context, all scoped to the operator's ADOM.
            • Icon picker in Plugin Studio and Report Studio (request: "the Builder and Plugin Studio must have the same icon menu, otherwise importing something can fail — bring the Builder's icon picker into Plugin Studio"). The app Settings tab and the Report Studio editor get SATOM Builder's picker: a searchable grid of the 2048 icons of the vendored Bootstrap Icons 1.11.3 font that a package may carry, served by GET /studio/icons.json — the same font and pattern the Builder builds its list from.

            Changed

            • Knowledge packs are kbpacks: satom-kbpack-YYYYMMDD[.N].tar.gz (request: "the API pack stays the API pack; the knowledge one must stop saying API pack: call it kbpack"). The file of the rolling knowledge lane was named like an API pack (satom-apipack-kb-...). Its version is still kb-YYYYMMDD[.N]; only the file name changes. The old name is still read everywhere (upload, feed, satom execute apipack import), and an upload or a feed download under it is stored as satom-kbpack-..., so a node shows one name for one pack. A schema /2 pack named satom-kbpack-* whose manifest is not of the knowledge lane is refused. The knowledge feed may name the kbpack in a kbpack block (file, url, sha256, size, sha256_url) that wins over the top-level file, which stays the old name for nodes on 4.6.0 and older. New provenance strings read pack:knowledge:satom-kbpack-...; rows written before keep theirs. The page says kbpack where it said knowledge pack (satom-harvester); the pack card is API packs & kbpacks.
            • One Upload for the three files (request: "it should be one file upload that takes the three: the SATOM update, the kbpack and the API pack"). Settings › Software Update has an Upload card (POST /self-update/upload, user_manage) that routes the file by its name: satom-update-<version>.tar.gz to the offline package staging and its preflight, satom-apipack-<version>.tar.gz and satom-kbpack-<date>.tar.gz to the pack list; any other name is refused and nothing is written. The separate upload forms of Offline update package and the pack card point to it; their routes stay for scripts.
            • Software Update fits a laptop screen (request: "check every card, they don't look right at my resolution"). API library packs lists its packs as one table across the whole card (pack, lane, source, size) instead of a narrow column of 47 rows next to an empty one; the pack detail and Recent imports (now with column headers) use the full width too. Knowledge packs stacks Installed and Available from the feed, so the installed table no longer runs under the Check now button, and the Scheduled fetch select is no longer cut. Recent updates says what each request was in a What column (a service restart, an OS-package check, a library upgrade, an offline package or a code revision) where Target was blank for everything but code updates.
            • Only the newest API pack of each series is listed (request: "keep only the latest; there is no need to keep the others — add a button to purge the old ones"). Older shipped packs are counted under the table, not listed; a release payload already carries only its own. New Purge old packs (N) button (POST /self-update/apipack/purge, user_manage): deletes every uploaded pack that a newer one of the same series replaces, keeps the newest of each series, never touches shipped packs; one apipack.delete audit row per pack.
            • The HA link card appears only where there is an HA pair (request: "if there is no HA, that card should not appear"): in HA mode with a standby registered, and on the standby. A failed check is still shown.
            • An Apps only account's menu is Plugins with its apps, already open (request: "only what is inside Plugins should appear, already expanded"). The portal pages (/a/ and every app page) draw a left menu holding only the apps the account may use, filed under their menu groups, every group open and without a toggle; no other console section, no bookmarks.
            • Plugin Studio's Explorer is a tree; the "Open an app" list is gone (request: "remove that section and make the menus there expandable"). Apps, Data stores, Connections and API Catalog have a caret that unfolds their items, each a link to its page; Apps unfold by menu group, each group folding on its own. It works as an accordion (follow-up request: "when a submenu opens the others should collapse, and the menu we are in should be highlighted"): opening an entry, by a click on it or on its caret, shows its pane, highlights it and folds the others; the entry of the pane you are on is drawn open, and one menu group is open at a time. Below 1400 px the Explorer stays the one-line strip of tabs, without the items. The Menu group filter of Apps is always shown (it used to appear only once a group existed, so it looked missing). An app or menu-group name cut by its ellipsis, in the Explorer or in the sidebar, shows whole in a small panel on hover (request: "on mouse over, show the full text in a little window"); an Explorer item used to show its slug there.
            • User guide §33 rewritten as Scout — the operations assistant: tools, the troubleshooting workflow, provider choice, what every exchange leaves behind, and what is planned. §13 describes Path Diagnostics, its saved reports and its metrics panel.
            • Plugin Studio tables, CSV downloads and copies leave out columns whose name starts with _ (the app's own ids and row buttons), as Save to a data store already did.
            • Installing an example creates all of its apps before saving any, so an app may open another app of the same bundle.

            Fixed

            • The bookmarks rail showed every device to accounts that may not see the inventory (security; request: "external users must see only their app; user sec sees a lot of Global, including the bookmarks"). The rail is open to every console account, and the device query it used scopes by ADOM and maintenance only, so a profile with no permission at all read every device's name and address in its grouping lens and in the add bookmark picker, while the dashboard told it "Your profile does not include viewing appliances". The lens, the picker and device bookmarks now need View appliances (appliances.view).

            • API Tokens: the pickers no longer cover the whole screen (request: "the selectors are not formatted for SATOM, they take the whole screen"). The menus sit on a fixed popper so they escape the card, and a fixed box sized at 100% is as wide as the window: every open picker (capabilities, AppIDs, apps) ran over the sidebar. Each menu now opens as wide as its own button, on the page and in the Edit dialog. The empty Processes it may run picker, left over from the removed Process section, is gone, and the Apps it may run picker now says how to hold a token to one app: tick only that app (app_arm never adds an app; it only lets granted apps run armed).

            • Deleting a directory connection now deletes its secret from the vault. With the vault as the secret store, a removed AD, LDAP or RADIUS connection left its bind password or shared secret under directory/<id>, where nothing read it any more. The vault copy now goes first; a vault that refuses the delete leaves the connection in place and says so.

            • App sign-in: what makes a FortiAuthenticator name a group, measured. On FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 the Access-Accept carries a group's Fortinet-Group-Name when the group has it as a RADIUS attribute and is in the group filter of the realm that accepted the user; a group outside that filter sends nothing, even for a member. The help text said it depended on the RADIUS client; the rule is no longer marked unverified.
            • Metric values lost precision on the way to the store. Every value was written with %g, which keeps six significant digits: a byte counter in the hundreds of millions was stored rounded to the nearest thousand, so rates over it moved in steps. Values are now written with 15 significant digits.
            • Deleting an appliance closes its live Sentinel incidents (open, verifying, mitigated) with a note naming the device. They used to stay open forever, out of every screen and every close button, and counted as open by the sweep (three of a device deleted in August). The three existing ones were closed the same way.
            • The syslog receiver names the senders it drops. The page said only "N unknown_source"; it now lists each dropped address with its count and last message, and says when the address belonged to a de-registered device that still has this receiver as its syslog target (found: a lab FortiWeb removed on 2026-10-24, still sending every ~3 minutes).
            • Scout saved a tool call as its answer when it reached the round limit still asking for a tool; the reply is now an answer, or a sentence saying the rounds ran out.
            • An icon name the font does not draw (bi-shield-search matches the bi-… pattern and shows as a blank) is no longer accepted silently. Saving a Plugin Studio app refuses it; a Report Studio save keeps the body and falls back to bi-puzzle with a warning (until now it stored any text, unchecked); importing a view, widget or app package never fails on its icon — it falls back to the default and the import report says so.
            • A refused app package import left objects behind. The helpers that create an app, a data store, a connection or an API version commit on their own, so a refusal raised after them (an action that opens an app the server does not have, a form field reading a data store that is nowhere) left them on the server — importing dns-lb-lookup before dns-records left an empty draft app dns-lb-lookup. The import now checks the form, diagram, actions and design against this server before it writes anything (what the package brings counts as present) and says which app to import first.
            • Changing Scout in Settings → AI → Scout ▸ Providers now leaves a row in the Audit Log: settings.ai_flags, settings.ai_provider_save (kind, base URL, model and whether a key was set, never the key), settings.ai_default and settings.ai_provider_delete. Until now, which endpoint the assistant sends to could change with no trace.
            • Scout runs a tool call the model wrote as bare JSON at the start of its reply (no fence), and drops anything written after it. Measured with a local model that wrote the call and then invented the result; SATOM ran nothing and the invented data reached the operator as the answer. The round goes back to the model as the call alone, never as its own text.
            • Scout no longer saves an empty reply as a successful answer. A reasoning model can stop after its hidden reasoning with no text; the round is retried once, and twice empty is an error the operator sees and the request ledger records as failed.
            • User guide §33 named the old Scout ladder Fault Isolation (§12); it is Path Diagnostics (§13), and it never calls Scout's AI providers.
